wedge.note: above mu 0.36 the nose simply stays where it is on the ramp: it is never driven inward

alternative_one_per_slider.each: o 3 x 0.3, free 21.2, k 0.2 (E), tab + bar pocket 10 deep, seated on the rib face
alternative_one_per_slider.one_spring_fails: that bolt has NO return force: it can sit retracted (one bolt holds the pack)
alternative_one_per_slider.why_not: a broken or lost spring leaves one bolt dead instead of both at half force; each spring sits on the slider's centre line (no squaring couple); the 4.0 rib carries a standing preload on each face (PCTG creep) and its seats are 1.0 deep at most

spring.chosen: two in parallel between the tabs: either one failing leaves both bolts sprung at half force (1.02 x the 35 g inertia), no standing load on the rib, a squaring couple on each slider

+y (away from the head).path: nub on the wedge foot -> rib -> cross walls; positive, self-locking for mu > 0.27
+y (away from the head).holds_note: with no wedge friction at all; no limit at mu 0.3

-y (onto the head).path: rim bands on the four heel pads; positive

+-x (across).path: pad friction, then the head's blade springs (each blade is sprung on its own: not positive)

+-z (along the pack).path: pad + wedge friction; positive stop: the nub on the tab arch

blade_entry.chamfers_beyond: recess mouth 1.0, tab plate edge 1.0: a blade up to 2.0 across still cams in (not swept)

error_budget.takes: clean to 0.9 across, 2.2 along; chamfers cam a blade in to 2.0 across
error_budget.v6: +-1.0 across, +-1.0 along (rest-stop lugs 1.0 from the blade)
error_budget.note: across: the worst case (2.1 mm) needs the chamfers; the head should float +-1 across (the head research's item 4)

error_budget.note: each blade is sprung on its own, so an offset across does not change either bolt's draw

error_budget.v6: not counted: nub, foot, blade over 1.0

error_budget.note: across is friction + the blade springs

slider.note: v6: flat blade face on two tab legs 1.6 wide and a 0.4 strip over the arch (centroid y 3.5); 1 mm off along the pack the contact is 2.6 / 0.6 wide on the legs: 3.4 off centre; past 1.0 the blade meets a rest-stop lug

spring_column.guide: its slot along the bolt, with a 2 x 7 printed pin inside (v6: none; open slots under the pack)

parts.XT60: 57 N to unmate is the project's own reading (the head research note); the spec sheet says 18 to 44 N

install.step: 1 a magnet into each bolt's underside
install.how: pressed in by hand, before the bolt goes in

install.step: 2 each bolt in through its wall hole, from outside
install.how: straight in, 30 mm swept; also with the pack already in

install.step: 3 stop bar down across the rib, into both bolts
install.how: straight down from above, 20 mm swept, bolts held at rest

install.step: 4 four springs, each with its guide pin, into the bolts' slots
install.how: squeezed to 14.6 mm and dropped in from above (slot 3.2 wide, spring 3.0)

install.step: 5 pack down into the cartridge (over the bolts, springs and stop bar)
install.how: straight down, 20 mm swept (the 0.6 keeper lips snap over it, not counted)
bolts held in, 40 mm swept; pushed in alone the lead-ins cam the bolts (no stuck step)

build.serviceable: a bolt comes out the way it went in once the pack, springs and stop bar are lifted out; nothing is glued
